key_insight: Graph-based mapping paired with fast routing can reduce transpilation costs while scaling to distributed superconducting quantum hardware with restricted connectivity.
engineering_relevance: The approach addresses both inter-module and intra-module routing, making it relevant to compiling circuits for realistically constrained multi-QPU systems.
method: Represent circuit interactions with a quantum interaction graph (QIG).
Use graph partitioning to map qubits across modules.
Apply a fast SABRE-inspired routing heuristic.
evidence_signal: On 48-qubit hardware, reported average aggregated-cost reductions reach 24.72% versus DMapS, with >250× speed-ups for structured workloads; on 399-qubit IBM Flamingo, runtimes remain practical, and structured routing-cost reductions versus DQC-adapted SABRE reach 51.96%.
watch_item: Reported gains depend on workload, topology, and cost model; the abstract does not establish improved execution fidelity on physical hardware.
paper_title: Scalable Transpilation for Overcoming Restricted Connectivity in Distributed Superconducting Quantum Architectures
